walkthroughs.body_html:
Systematic Approach To Problem Solving — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Systematic Approach To Problem Solving brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Systematic Approach To Problem Solving.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Hoare's quicksort algorithm was published in:

options: O(log n)
O(n)

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
options: O(log n).
It can store data permanently.

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: It can explode or be damaged easily.
O(1) - because it is fast.
Its contents are lost when power is removed.
It can store data permanently.

mcqs.q: What is hexadecimal A in denary?
options: It can store data permanently.
1 (treating A as the first letter).
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
